title: An AI can help write a voxel game. Can it actually play one? Our VentiKenny workflow.
author: Temporary_Ad3420
selftext:
I’m developing VentiKenny at ByronInsight AG: a free Unreal Engine/C++ voxel sandbox with building, exploration, bosses, parkour and two story adventures. We also use it as a practical test environment for AI software agents.



The interesting part for this community is the boundary between the agent and the game. C++ handles steering, jumping, aiming, placement timing and combat at frame rate. The external agent chooses a bounded goal, reads the reported result, then decides what to do next. That keeps input timing out of a slow language-model round trip.



For building, the play workflow requires the same kind of actions as a player: select a block, aim at a supporting face, stay within reach and place it. A bridge created by writing terrain coordinates would not count as evidence that an agent can build a bridge.



Each play session has a learning loop: read earlier lessons, record failures and observations, write a run journal, then promote useful lessons into the next session’s instructions. We also check a live heartbeat and command acknowledgements so a stale state file cannot masquerade as a successful action.



This is a development workflow, not a claim that agents have mastered the game. The trailer shows the game itself, not an autonomous-agent benchmark.



Gameplay trailer: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cr8F6ZIL8QI](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cr8F6ZIL8QI)



If you want to try the game, Windows and macOS downloads are free: [https://ventikenny.itch.io/ventikenny?utm\_source=reddit&utm\_medium=community&utm\_campaign=aigamedev\_workflow\_20261102](https://ventikenny.itch.io/ventikenny?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=community&utm_campaign=aigamedev_workflow_20261102)



For those building similar environments: what would you measure to distinguish an agent that learned to play from one that merely exploited its tooling?



Disclosure: I’m affiliated with the game. Generative AI tools are used for code and graphics, and assisted in preparing this post.
